title: nushell: str downcase deprecation warning in completion.nu
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have read through the manual page (`man fzf`)
- [x] I have searched through the existing issues
- [x] For bug reports, I have checked if the bug is reproducible in the latest version of fzf

### Output of `fzf --version`

0.73.1

### OS

- [x] Linux
- [ ] macOS
- [ ] Windows
- [ ] Etc.

### Shell

- [ ] bash
- [ ] zsh
- [ ] fish

### Problem / Steps to reproduce

```nu
Warning: nu::parser::deprecated

  ⚠ Command deprecated.
     ╭─[/nix/store/vxr7g2i5vcaasw1hr8baxjig55l83kgg-nushell-fzf-integration.nu:288:41]
 287 │       $ssh_configs | append $ssh_configs_d | append $ssh_config_global
 288 │                    | where {|it| ($it | str downcase | str starts-with 'host') or ($it | str downcase | str starts-with 'hostname') }
     ·                                         ──────┬─────
     ·                                               ╰── str downcase was deprecated in 0.114.0 and will be removed in a future release.
 289 │                    | parse --regex '^\s*host(?:<nick>)?\s+(?<hosts>.+)' # Extract hosts after keyword
     ╰────
  help: Use `str lowercase` instead.
```

comments.author: participant2
participant2
comments.body:
Substituting for `lowercase` with user message could look something like this for a Nushell<0.114.0 user:
```
Error: nu::parser::extra_positional

  × Extra positional argument.
     ╭─[/home/<user>/.config/nushell/autoload/_fzf_integration.nu:287:45]
 286 │                      # NOTE: str lowercase is new from Nushell 0.114.0. Please upgrade to Nushell >=0.114.0 if you are seeing `extra positional argument` error regarding `str lowercase` in this block.
 287 │                    | where {|it| ($it | str lowercase | str starts-with 'host') or ($it | str lowercase | str starts-with 'hostname') }
     ·                                             ────┬────
     ·                                                 ╰── extra positional argument
 288 │                    | parse --regex '^\s*host(?:<nick>)?\s+(?<hosts>.+)' # Extract hosts after keyword
     ╰────
  help: Usage: str
```

Notice the `# NOTE` comment that is taken straight from the file by the compiler. I don't think there's another way to show an error message since the compiler makes a first pass before executing anything in the file and that is when it displays the error. Any attempt to use an instruction to display a message will not work. So, the comment is just a little hack I found to do it...

I implemented it in 4f7b79c, but I can't open a PR since I'm not a ~contributor~collaborator.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> Note that this is only used in the ssh completion code.

Given this, I'd prefer the simpler approach, let me cherry-pick your commit. Thanks!

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Oh, the error message always appears during load if you have an old version of nushell, not only when you use `ssh` completion.

Then, I think we should take the `__fzf_str_lowercase_impl` approach you showed above. The extra delay only applies to `ssh` completion. If you push the fix to your fork, I'll cherry-pick it.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
OK. I implemented it in 4ea65a3.

NOTE: On my machine, executing the function yields this run duration for 38 ssh addresses:

```nushell
>: timeit { __fzf_list_hosts }
1sec 290ms 502µs 637ns
```

compared to the original:

```nushell

```

Thanks, but whoa, I didn't expect it to be that slow. I thought it would only add a few tens of milliseconds. A full second is a deal-breaker, so I'll stick with the previous one.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: Working around this with: `fzf --nushell | str replace --all 'str downcase' 'str lowercase' | ...`

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
Maybe using [`try/catch`](https://www.nushell.sh/commands/docs/try.html) could work here?

> I see that this happened in [0.114.0](https://www.nushell.sh/blog/2026-07-04-nushell_v0_114_0.html#deprecate-str-upcase-str-downcase-and-add-str-uppercase-str-lowercase). However, there is also some [annoying bug](https://github.com/nushell/nushell/issues/18528) right now with 0.114.0. I was able to test the fix to `lowercase` instead and it works. However, do we want to force the change to `lowercase` or do we want to use the appropriate command depending on the version? The latter approach would make the switch to 0.114.0 easier for anybody using the nushell FZF integration.
> 
> The only implementation I managed to make work is this one:
> 
> let __fzf_str_lowercase_impl = if ((version | get major) == 0 and (version | get minor) < 114) {
>   "str downcase"
> } else {
>   "str lowercase"
> }
> 
> def __fzf_str_lowercase []: string -> string {
>   $in | nu --commands $"\"($in)\" | ($__fzf_str_lowercase_impl)"
> }
> 
> However, this calls a subshell each time we call this function, so it slows it down a bit. Note that this is only used in the ssh completion code.
> 
> Writing a closure with variable definition doesn't work since the closure would need to compile in both versions, but it can't.
> 
> I don't like either of the solutions. But I'm guessing that the simplest would be best. Just simply substitute `downcase` with `lowercase` and may be tell the user to update to Nushell 0.114.0 to make it work.
> 
> [@participant1](https://github.com/participant1): do you agree?

comments.author: participant2
participant3
comments.body: We could conditionally source a file containing version-compatible functionality, but I'm not sure how/if that would work with `go:embed`.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: But at this point, it starts being a bit too complex, just for a small retro-compatibility feature, doesn't it?

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: Fair enough. For once, I'd support breaking backwards compatibility here and switching to `str lowercase`, seeing as nushell issues a disclaimer outright saying that it is subject to breaking changes at this point.
